analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side text of CHANGELOG.md (lines 4539-5345), historical release notes. The patch excerpt shows a documentation-only change: it replaces the v0.10.9 candidate header with v0.10.10 and adds notes on waitlists (darkbloom waitlist, an approval gate for new sandbox setup and new cluster pairs). It touches no source code, protocol, crypto, attestation or storage logic. The excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the v0.10.10 text is not visible. Security-relevant claims in the visible notes: (1) new Darkbloom Sandbox setup and new two-Mac pairs need account approval, enforced by the coordinator waitlist. That enforcement is a platform-side control outside this repo's evidence. (2) Existing setups are grandfathered. (3) If the coordinator does not offer waitlists yet, both new setups proceed as before, a fail-open fallback by design. This is a product gating policy, not a security boundary in the threat model (TB-013 and TB-014 concern installer integrity and root GPU-limit changes, which are unchanged). `darkbloom cluster local` needs no approval. The base text is older historical changelog entries, including the SSD prefix-cache notes relevant to T-041, and none of it is modified. The wording of the visible notes is consistent with the existing T-041 posture (encrypted SSD, HMAC-keyed names, scoped salts, 30-minute TTL), so no threat-model drift is evident. I identified no regression. Remaining questions for integration: the actual code implementing the waitlist client (outside this batch) should be checked for whether the fail-open path when the coordinator lacks waitlist support could bypass gating that is meant to be security-relevant, and whether the waitlist calls use authenticated, TLS-protected requests.
